keyGuarantees: the settlement is dead and graded relic_ruin by the lifecycle writer
pools.ruling: Not scoped: a dead town speaks of departure, never of a live calm; line 1 presumes how the residents left (history facts).

lines.text: {settlement} has died, and its stones stand as a relic ruin; the last residents left with the wagons, their fates unresolved. The interior is yours.
Nothing is recorded at {settlement} any more. The rolls close on a departure and not on a disaster, and where the people went is not written. The interior is yours.
What stands at {settlement} is worth walking into and no longer worth living in; those who left, left together, and their fates are unresolved. The interior is yours.
The country around {settlement} still uses the name, and uses it for the place rather than for the people.

keyGuarantees: the settlement is dead and graded abandoned_site by the lifecycle writer
pools.ruling: Not scoped: a dead town speaks of departure, never of a live calm; line 1 presumes how the residents left (history facts).

lines.text: {settlement} has died, and a quiet site marks where it stood; the last residents left with the wagons, their fates unresolved.
{settlement} is off the rolls. What remains is ground with a name on it and nothing standing worth the name.
There is less at {settlement} than a ruin: a shape in the ground, and the memory of a shape; those who left it, left it whole, and their fates are unresolved.
People still give directions past {settlement}, which is more than the place itself still offers.

keyGuarantees: history.ancientRuin carries a proper name (a fallen city near the town)
pools.ruling: Not scoped: speaks of the past; two lines presume local superstition, which has no reader (culture).

lines.text: The relic ruin of {ruin} stands near {settlement}, a city that fell {timeband_since} and has been drawing superstition ever since. Its interior is yours.
{ruin} fell {timeband_since} and {settlement} has grown up in its shadow; what the older place was is not remembered here, only that it was larger. Its interior is yours.
{settlement} does not go into {ruin}, and the not-going is a rule nobody has ever had to write down.
{ruin} is {timeband_age} and appears on no roll of {settlement}'s; the ground it stands on is claimed by nobody and worked by nobody.

lines.text: {steading} holds {band} and works {resource} for {settlement}.
{steading} is {band} of people and one reason to be there, and the reason is {resource}.
{steading} is close enough to {settlement} to be counted and far enough to be its own place.

lines.text: {steading} holds {band} and was founded by decree rather than by settlement; {settlement}'s hall put it where it is and put people in it.
{steading} exists because {settlement} decided it should, which is a different origin from every other place on this list and shows in how it is run.
Nobody moved to {steading}. They were sent, and {band} of them are still there.

keyGuarantees: one satellite steading awaiting its charter
pools.ruling: Colour: per-steading rows presume nothing beyond the row.

lines.text: {steading} holds {band} and has no charter yet; what it is entitled to is being decided at {settlement}.
{steading} is a place before it is a settlement. The people are there, the charter is not, and the gap is where the arguments are.
{steading} does not know yet what it will be allowed to become.
